config.title: Settings
config.identityIntro: The key your watermarks are signed with. It belongs to you, not to a database, and is created by itself the first time you mark a file.
config.identityNone: No identity yet — one will be created the first time you export a file with its origin. You can also create it now by saving it.
config.identityWarning: The saved file lets anyone holding it sign in your name. Do not share it.
config.identityPassphraseNeeded: This file is protected: enter its passphrase above, then try again.
config.identityRegenerateWarning: This revokes nothing. Files you have already marked carry the key they were signed with and keep verifying for ever — including any signed by someone who obtained your identity file. What protects you after a leak is publishing your new fingerprint and disowning the old one.
config.identityRegenerateKeep: The current key ({fingerprint}) will be overwritten. Save it first if you may need it.
config.libraryNoDatabase: These settings belong to a library. Open a database to see them.
config.thresholdsIntro: An error, then the blunder an error becomes: the two lines this library draws, in equity. Every blunder is an error, so the first threshold cannot exceed the second. They follow the file, not the machine.
config.thresholdPresetsIntro: Every program has drawn its own line. Here are theirs:
config.bearoffIntro: Two-sided bearoff database: exact winning probability and cube verdict in the Eval panel. Nothing is downloaded and nothing is embedded — the tables are computed here, on this machine, and checked against gnubg's fingerprint. The two default tables are made on first launch, in the background.
config.bearoffWiderNote: A wider table covers bearoff positions with more chequers per player. Pick the domain: its size, its memory and its time on this machine are stated before you commit.
config.bearoffCost: {size} on disk, {ram} of memory, about {time} on {cores} cores.
config.bearoffCostSequential: {size} on disk, {ram} of memory, about {time} on one core.
config.bearoffPurposeOneSided: Gives the EPC when a chequer is outside the home board.
config.bearoffTooBig: This machine cannot compute it: it would need {ram} of memory, {available} are left.
config.bearoffEstimateUnmeasured: (estimate; the real time is measured on the first run)
config.vacuumIntro: Compacting rewrites the file to reclaim space left behind by deletions (matches, tournaments, purges). Needs roughly twice the current size in free disk space; can take a while on a large database.
config.vacuumConfirm: Compacting the database can take a while and needs roughly twice its size in free disk space. Continue?
config.logsIntro: The log file records diagnostic details useful when reporting a problem.
config.gammonnetIntro: Settings for the embedded gammonNet evaluator: display depth and analysis depth are two separate settings — lowering the display never degrades what the analysis batch writes to the database.
config.gammonnetDisplayPlyNote: Interactive comfort while editing the board. Never written to the database.
config.gammonnetAnalysisPlyNote: What the post-import analysis batch writes into a position's Analysis.
config.gammonnetAutoAnalyzeNote: After importing a match with no analysis, runs a bounded, cancellable background analysis of positions still missing a gammonNet analysis.
config.gammonnetCatchUpUnknown: Checking for positions without an analysis…
config.gammonnetCatchUpNote: Runs the same bounded, cancellable analysis manually — useful to catch up a library built before this feature existed.
config.gammonnetStaleNote: Re-runs gammonNet on positions it already analyzed, but written with an older engine version or a different depth than configured here — XG, GNUbg and BGBlitz analyses are never touched.
config.metNote: gammonNet values match scores with this table, and every analysis it computes records it. An analysis at a match score computed with another table is marked "different MET" and left out of the statistics. Changing the table rewrites no analysis. Only explicit gnubg tables are read.
config.metBuiltInImported: This file is Kazaross-XG2, the built-in table: nothing was added.
config.checkForUpdatesNote: Queries GitHub's release page once at startup. Off by default, and never enabled automatically on a package-managed install (Flatpak, a distro package, Homebrew…).
config.repairIntro: Recomputes the analysis columns from the analyses themselves. Those columns are a projection of the stored data, which stays intact: a fault in the projection is repairable without re-importing anything. Explicit and never automatic.
config.repairConfirm: Recompute the analysis columns of the whole database?
config.watchIntro: blunderDB can look at a folder while it runs and import each match file that appears in it. Nothing is guessed: until a folder is named, there is no watch.
config.watchSuggestLabel: Look for a match folder on this machine
config.watchNoSuggestion: No known match folder was found on this machine; name it yourself.
config.watchIntervalNote: 0 keeps the default, ten seconds; the floor is two. A file is imported only once its size has settled, so a half-written match is never read.
config.watchOnlyNewNote: Only files that APPEAR are imported: whatever the folder already holds is ignored. To import that, use the folder import.
config.themeNote: The theme sets the interface colours and proposes a board palette. You keep the last word: the Colours tab still sets the board, and your setting survives the theme.
config.likeNote: Zero: no ceiling. The token like<12 sets its own for one search.
config.commentAuthorNote: Signs the comments you write. Empty: unsigned.

general.title: General tour
general.desc: A quick overview of the interface.

welcome.title: Welcome to blunderDB
welcome.body: A quick tour of the interface. Press Esc to exit.

toolbar.title: Toolbar
toolbar.body: Databases, imports, navigation, settings and help.

board.title: The board
board.body: Edit positions here: click to place checkers, set the dice, cube and score.

panels.title: Panels
panels.body: Analysis, comments, search, stats, collections, matches and tournaments.

commandline.title: Command line
commandline.body: Press Space for the command line. Type 's' to search, '?' for help.

done.title: All set!
done.body: Replay tours from the cap icon, or the 'tutorial' command.

search.title: Searching positions
search.desc: Find positions by structure, filters and stats.

intro.title: Searching
intro.body: Find positions by structure, filters and statistics.

tab.title: Search filters
tab.body: Combine filters: pip count, checkers, scores, win rates, dice and more.

structure.title: By structure
structure.body: Set up a position to find others with the same structure.

commandline.title: Command line
commandline.body: Or press Space and type, e.g. 's w>50 p>30'. '?' lists the filters.

intro.title: Matches
intro.body: Import full matches (XG, GnuBG, BGBlitz) and review them.

tab.title: Your matches
tab.body: Imported matches, with PR and MWC loss per player.

review.title: Step through
review.body: Pick a match to replay its moves and study the blunders.

intro.title: Tournaments
intro.body: Group matches into tournaments to track your performance.

tab.title: Your tournaments
tab.body: Manage events and review per-player results.

drill.title: Drill down
drill.body: Jump from a tournament to its matches and positions.

eval.title: Eval panel
eval.desc: Evaluate the position on the board.

intro.title: Evaluating a position
intro.body: blunderDB carries its own evaluator: you do not need an imported analysis to know what a position is worth.

tab.title: The Eval tab
tab.body: Ctrl+E. It gives the best move, the cube decision and the effective pip count (EPC).

position.title: The position being evaluated
position.body: Always the one on the board: set the checkers, the dice and the score, and the evaluation follows.

scale.title: Money or match
scale.body: At money play equity is in points; at a score it is normalised — ±1 is the current cube won or lost.

anki.title: Anki review
anki.desc: Review your positions by spaced repetition.

intro.title: Reviewing your mistakes
intro.body: A review deck turns the positions you got wrong into cards and shows them again at the right moment.

tab.title: The Anki tab
tab.body: Ctrl+K. Build a deck here, review it, and follow what is left to see.

deck.title: Building a deck
deck.body: A deck starts from a search or a collection: it resynchronises as the database changes.

review.title: Answering a card
review.body: The answer stays hidden until you ask for it; your grade sets the next due date.

stats.title: Statistics
stats.desc: Read your level and your progress.

intro.title: Measuring your play
intro.body: Statistics cover the matches imported with their analysis — that is where the level shows.

tab.title: The Stats tab
tab.body: Ctrl+D. Four views: dashboard, errors, progression and players.

pr.title: The PR
pr.body: The average error per decision, in millipoints. Lower is better; it compares with XG's.

filters.title: Narrowing the measure
filters.body: Period, opponent, match length, tournament: every filter recomputes the whole table.

stats.planHint: Error families (plan of play × theme) ranked by recoverable MWC: the loss beyond what a reference player would lose in the same positions, with its 95% interval. A family enters the plan from {n} errors and an interval above zero.
stats.planEmpty: No error priced in MWC in this filter.
stats.planNoEvidence: No family has enough errors to be ranked yet.
stats.planQuizFirst: Quiz on the first three families
stats.planOutside: Outside the plan: {unthemed} errors without a theme, {unpriced} unpriced (money play, missing options).
stats.effectHint: For each error family one of whose positions you studied (marked studied, reviewed in Anki, answered in a quiz): the MWC lost per 100 decisions of its plan and kind, in the matches played before the day of the first study action and in those played after it. Gain = before − after, with its 95% interval; a direction is stated only with {n} decisions on each side and an interval that excludes zero.
stats.effectEmpty: No family studied yet: mark positions studied, review them in Anki or answer them in a quiz.
stats.effectUnstudied: {n} families of the filter not studied yet.
stats.effectCaveat: A change, not an effect: a family is studied because it cost, so part of any gain is regression to the mean; nothing here controls for the opponents, the format or the dice.
stats.biasesHint: Which way your decisions err: the share erring one way minus the share erring the other, with its 95% interval. A lean is named only with {n} decisions and an interval that excludes zero.
stats.biases_blots_minus: more cautious than the best play
stats.biasesUnread: {n} of {total} checker plays with contact ({share}) could not be replayed and are left out of the blots bias.
stats.biasesByScore: Doubles by score (your away – opponent’s away)
stats.biasesByScoreEmpty: No score has {n} doubling decisions yet.
stats.timeErrorsHint: Per player, the decisions with a recorded time, by how long they took: how many, the mean error in millipoints, and the share of blunders. A decision with no stored error is counted but not averaged.
stats.recurringHint: Your errors in the current filter, grouped by plan of play and theme, costliest first. The cost is the share of the PR a group accounts for. Click a group to open its positions.
stats.contrastButton: Positions played well by one and not the other
stats.contrastSummary: {n} of {total} common positions: {a} played {na} well, {b} played {nb} well.
stats.contrastEmpty: None of the {total} common positions was played well by one and not the other.
stats.contrastUnscored: {n} plays of these two players are not scored yet and are left out: plays are scored only on request.
stats.trainingHint: The Decision quiz PR, the PR of the filter's matches and the Anki retention, on the same calendar windows. The quiz PR is on the real PR's scale; the retention reads on the right axis (%). In brackets, the number of decisions or reviews: a window with no sample has no value.
stats.trainingEmpty: No quiz session, no match and no Anki review yet.
stats.trainingThemes: Quiz PR by plan of play
stats.trainingThemesHint: Decisions of the Decision quiz drawn from library positions, worst first.
stats.compareColumnHint: Tick two players to compare their figures
stats.playersColPRHint: PR: average error per decision, in millipoints (mp); lower is better
stats.playersColLuckHint: Luck: average dice effect per roll, in mp; positive = favourable dice
stats.engineHint: Keep only the decisions analysed by this engine (gnubg, xg…)
stats.minDepthHint: Keep only the decisions analysed at least this deep (plies)

corpus.h2hNone: No match between these two players for this filter.

stats.intervalHint: 95 % confidence interval: resamples the matches of a selection, the games of a match. A row without one (fewer than three matches or games, or all at the same PR) is greyed.
stats.breakdownOpenBlunders: Open the {n} positions with a blunder ({decisions} blunders)
stats.breakdownCountsMissing: Row missing from the position counts
stats.breakdownBlundersHint: Positions where at least one decision is a blunder
stats.planOutsideShort: Outside the plan: {unthemed} without a theme · {unpriced} unpriced

home.title: blunderDB
home.lede: Your backgammon position database: import your matches, search for what you want to look at again, measure what you play.
home.importNote: A fresh database, your XG, GNU Backgammon, Jellyfish or BGBlitz files, and your PR with your worst decisions in two minutes.
home.demoNote: Three matches, collections, comments and an Anki deck: enough to try everything without bringing anything.
home.tourNote: A walk through the interface, panel by panel.
home.dismiss: Carry on without opening a database

report.title: blunderDB report
report.noBlunder: No faulty decision in this scope.
report.footer: Self-contained document produced by blunderDB. Print it to PDF from your browser.
report.failed: The report could not be produced: {err}

training.title: Training
training.gradeFailed: The answer could not be graded.
training.playOnBoard: Play the move on the board, then click the dice.
training.faultHint: Click the number you got wrong.
training.noQuestion: No question can be asked: this library or this source provides none.

numbers.evalWin: Win chance of the player on roll (%)

training.toleranceEvaluation: Tolerance: five points on the win chance; the cube action is graded exactly.

refusal.notBearoff: This exercise needs a bear-off: both sides entirely in their home board.
refusal.tooFewCheckers: This exercise needs 4 to 15 chequers a side, the rest borne off.
refusal.emptyBoard: The board is empty: the question comes from the pool.

refusal.notAGame: This exercise needs a game position: fifteen chequers a side, and neither side fully borne off.
refusal.notMoneyCubeDecision: This exercise needs a money-game cube decision, with no dice and the cube centred or held by the player on roll: none was found in the browsed list.

training.truthExact: Truth: the two-sided bear-off database, exact.
training.scoresInstruction: For each box, work the number out in your head, then click Reveal. Afterwards, click every number you got wrong.

explain.blots: You lose {cost} mp: the move played leaves {blots} blots where {best} leaves only {bestBlots}.
explain.point: You lose {cost} mp: {best} makes a point in your home board that the move played does not.
explain.gammon: You lose {cost} mp: the move played gives up {gammon} points of gammon chances that {best} keeps.
explain.passive: You lose {cost} mp: the move played is safer, but {best} wins more often — safety costs more than it earns here.
explain.doubletoolate: You lose {cost} mp: this was a double, and you did not offer it ({best}).
explain.doubletooearly: You lose {cost} mp: the double is premature, {best}.
explain.taketooloose: You lose {cost} mp: the take is too loose, {best}.
explain.passtootight: You lose {cost} mp: the pass is too tight, {best}.

similar.noPosition: No current position to find neighbours of.
similar.failed: The search for close positions failed.
similar.none: No close position in this database.

log.title: Activity log
log.copyFailed: The log could not be copied.

contactSheet.title: Contact sheet
contactSheet.hint: Arrows, J and K: move · Home, End: ends of the page · Page Up, Page Down: change page · Enter: open the position
contactSheet.notInMatch: The contact sheet shows the browsed list, not a match: leave the match first.

named.suisse_tableauHint: Recommended for 16 to 32 players. Every loss counts the same, and the end resolves without a tie-break.
named.eliminationHint: The shortest format. One loss and the tournament is over.
named.consolanteHint: Losers from the main bracket play each other.
named.double_eliminationHint: It takes two losses to go out; the consolation winner plays the final again.
named.gslHint: Groups of four, paired by results: nothing depends on when a result is announced.
named.poulesHint: Everyone plays the same number of matches before the bracket.

settings.lengthHint: Number of points in a match of this phase.
settings.targetHint: Move to the bracket when the sum of remaining lives (players × lives) falls to this number. 0: no switch.
settings.finalLengthHint: Length of the final. 0: same as the other matches.
settings.unavailableHint: Numbers of the tables no longer to assign, separated by commas: a broken board, a table removed.
settings.frozen: The tournament has started: only the format of an open phase is frozen. Everything else can change, and every change is an event.
settings.deleteConfirm: Delete this tournament's direction? The tournament and its matches stay; the matches only lose the slot they filled.
settings.phaseOpened: The phase is open: its lives are already dealt.
settings.addPhaseHint: The phase is added after the others and does not interrupt the one under way.
settings.removePhaseHint: A phase already opened cannot be removed.
settings.breaksHint: Nothing is blocked: a match that would end during a break carries a warning, and you decide.
settings.batchHint: Pair in batches, every N minutes, so that the time a result is announced no longer picks the opponent. 0: as they come.
settings.lengthsHint: Length round by round, FROM THE LAST TO THE FIRST: “15, 13, 11” = final at 15, semis at 13, quarters at 11. Empty: the phase's length.
settings.lengthLateHint: Lengthen matches once only a few players are still alive. 0: never.
settings.lateThresholdHint: How many players still alive before matches lengthen.
settings.entryFeeHint: Per entrant. Everyone who entered counts, withdrawals included: they paid.
settings.retentionPercentHint: The share of the pool the club keeps.
settings.retentionAmountHint: A fixed amount the club keeps, on top of the percentage.
settings.scaleHint: One value per place, from the first to the last paid.
settings.percentHint: Ticked: percentages of the payable pool. Unticked: fixed amounts.
settings.seedingHint: Off by default: the engine's study concludes “no protected seeds”, which is the current culture of backgammon. On, players are placed by rating — the best and the second in opposite halves. The ⓘ button leads to the study.
settings.consolationHint: The losers of the bracket play a second bracket, a separate section in the standings.
settings.reconciliationHint: The consolation winner plays the main bracket winner (double elimination).
settings.rechargeHint: In double elimination, the main bracket winner must be beaten twice.
settings.consoScaleHint: The consolation has standings of its own only with a prize scale: fill in “Consolation” under Prize fund.
settings.qualifiersHint: Players per pool who go through to the next phase. Empty: 2.
settings.minPerPointHint: Planned duration of a point, in minutes: the clock strip compares the observed pace with it, and the estimated end starts from it. Empty: 8.
settings.swissSkipped: The Swiss phase would be skipped: {lives} lives at the start, for a switch at {target}. Lower the switch or add lives.

warning.bracket_wrong_players: Match {match} ({section}, {label}): {a} against {b}, but the bracket expects {expectedA} against {expectedB}.
warning.ends_in_break: Match {match}: its expected end falls during a break.
warning.slow_match: Match {match}: running beyond the expected time.
warning.table_shared: Table {table}: matches {other} and {match} are both running there.
warning.correction_eliminates_running: Match {match}: {player} has no life left since a correction, and is still playing.
warning.correction_revives: {player} regains a life after a correction: can be paired again.

proposals.keys: J / K or ↑ ↓: pick a proposal · Enter: launch it · ← →: move between tables
proposals.title: Proposals ({n})
proposals.allHint: Launch the whole queue at once.
proposals.appeared: {n} proposal(s) are waiting for you in the tournament.
proposals.repairHint: Cancel this match, made inconsistent by a correction. Nothing else moves: the correct restarts will be proposed next.

table.title: Tables ({n})
table.shared: Two matches on this table: move one

result.title: Result

players.name: Name
players.ratingHint: Entry PR: lower is better. Empty if unknown.
players.withdrawNowHint: Withdraw now: their running matches are lost by forfeit.
players.withdrawLaterHint: No longer paired, but finishes the match they are at.
players.reinstateHint: Reinstate them: they are paired again, with the results and lives they had when they left; matches lost by forfeit at their withdrawal stay lost.
players.absentHint: Absent for a while: no longer paired, but keeps their rank, lives and place — without withdrawing.
players.returnHint: Lift the absence: they are paired again right away.
players.slotHint: Where this player will enter. A free bye, or later: no draw is ever redone.
players.noEntry: {player} is entered but enters no phase.
players.pairHint: A doubles competition: two persons, one entrant "A / B".
players.pairRatingHint: The mean of the two ratings by default; a value typed here replaces it.
players.withdrawNowConfirm: Withdraw {name} from the tournament now? They will no longer be paired (can be reinstated).
players.withdrawLaterConfirm: Withdraw {name} after their match? They will not be paired afterwards (can be reinstated).

standings.closeConfirm: Matches under way: {n}. Closing freezes the standings without them: their result can no longer be entered, unless the tournament is reopened.
standings.tiedHint: Tied: the place and the prize are shared.
standings.reopenConfirm: Reopen this tournament? The final standings stop being final, and the reopening stays in the log.
standings.saveHint: Saves the standings to a CSV file, the same as the copy.
standings.historyHint: This player's history, to correct a result

clock.endHint: The engine's forecast at the planned pace, after the declared breaks. A night not declared as a break counts as play.

credit.title: About the engine
credit.by: Nicomaque, a tournament engine created by Nicolas Harmand.
credit.what: It holds the format, the pairings, the brackets and the standings; blunderDB gives it an interface and keeps its matches.

slots.noneSuggested: None of these matches carries both names of a slot: attach them by hand.

display.openFailed: Page written, but it could not be opened: {path}

sheet.hint: The round's pairing sheet, to put on the welcome desk. The print dialog opens by itself.

sheet.error: The pairing sheet could not be written.

sheet.announcedHint: The date and time printed on the sheet, as you type them.

assistant.mcpIntro: While blunderDB runs, it can offer its tools to an assistant (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, a local client) over the Model Context Protocol, on this machine only. Off by default.
assistant.mcpWriteNote: Unticked, the tools only read. Ticked, they may also save a position, comment on it, create and fill a collection; nothing deletes.
assistant.viewNeedsNormalMode: The assistant opens a view only in normal or edit mode.
assistant.title: In-app assistant
assistant.intro: Ask in one sentence: the assistant searches with the command bar's grammar and opens the result in a new view named after your sentence. It reads everywhere; any change is put to you before it is made. Off by default; no model is bundled.
assistant.keyStored: A key is stored in the system keyring.
assistant.keyNone: No key stored (not needed for Ollama).
assistant.privacyWarning: With {provider}, your sentences and the tool results (positions, statistics, player names) leave this machine for a remote service.
assistant.privacyAccept: I agree to send my sentences and the tool results to this provider
assistant.placeholder: Ask in one sentence… (Enter to send)
assistant.declined: declined by you; nothing was written
assistant.disabled: The assistant is off: turn it on in Settings › Assistant and MCP.
assistant.needsAck: First accept this provider's privacy warning in Settings › Assistant and MCP.
assistant.write: Let the assistant propose changes (each one confirmed)
